topic.situation: Nittaya, Amphon, and others were each allocated equal amounts of Kha Nii 117 rice seed. After the allocation, Amphon will take Nittaya's Kha Nii 117 seed, claiming it is to repay a debt she owes him.

part_1:
Amphon: Hello everyone. It's really crowded today, isn't it?

Nittaya: Yes, Amphon. A lot of people came to pick up the seed today.

Charoen: This Kha Nii 117 seed is really good; I've heard it's drought-tolerant.

Wichian: Yes, I've heard the yield is good too, so I rushed to get it.

Amphon: It's good we came early; otherwise the seeds will be gone.

Nittaya: That's right. I saw some people who came late and didn't get any.

Charoen: Where will we plant the seeds?

Wichian: I plan to plant them in the paddy fields near my home. The soil there is good.

Amphon: I think the same. I have some space at home that I can use.

Nittaya: That's great. If the results are good, I'll come pick some up next year.

Charoen: Yes, if it does well we'll tell our friends.

Wichian: Then let's go collect the seeds before they're gone.

Amphon: Let's go!

Amphon: Nittaya has seemed stressed lately.

Amphon: I've heard she's looking for new ways to manage her debts.

Charoen: I think she might try to find a side job or cut some expenses.

Amphon: Right. Consulting a financial advisor might help.

Charoen: I agree. Sometimes having someone to guide you reveals solutions you hadn't thought of.

Amphon: I hope she finds a solution soon.

Charoen: Me too. If we can help, we should tell her.

Amphon: Of course. We should help each other when a friend is in need.

Charoen: Yes, as friends we should support each other.

Charoen: That was quick.

Amphon: Good. Let's talk about dividing the seed.

Charoen: Yes. How should we divide the Kha Nii 117 seed?

Wichian: I think we should divide it according to how much land each person has.

Amphon: Agreed. Whoever has more land should get a bit more.

Charoen: What about those with small plots?

Wichian: We can allocate based on suitability, but everyone should get enough to plant.

Amphon: Okay, let's come to an agreement now.

Charoen: Yes, so we don't have to think about it later.

Wichian: Okay, but I need to step out for a moment.

Amphon: Alright, Wichian. See you later.

Charoen: See you.

Wichian: Thank you. I'll be back shortly.

Nittaya: Thank you. I'll remember that.

Narong: Yes. I've grown it before and the yield was great, so I planned to get some again this year.

Charoen: What do we need to do to receive the seed?

Amphon: I heard we need to register first, and bring our farmer ID card.

Nittaya: Yes, we should prepare the documents so we don't waste time when collecting.

Narong: Right. If you have all the documents ready, you'll get the seed faster.

Charoen: Great. I'll go register now then.

Amphon: I'll go with you so we don't waste time.

Charoen: Thanks a lot, Narong.

Amphon: Thank you.

Nittaya: Thank you, Narong.

Narong: No problem. We're friends, after all.

Nittaya: I also need to step out for privacy reasons. See you later.

Narong: Okay, see you later, Charoen and Nittaya.

Amphon: See you.

Amphon: All right, let's go.

Nittaya: Hello, I'm back.

Narong: Welcome back, Nittaya.

Amphon: You're back quickly.

Nittaya: Yes, I finished my personal matters quickly, so I'm back to look at the seed distribution.

Narong: Good timing. We were just discussing how to divide the Kha Nii 117 seed.

Narong: Yes. Managing it well will help everyone get the most benefit.

Amphon: Do you have a plan, Nittaya?

Charoen: Thank you so much, Narong. I really appreciate it.

Amphon: No problem. We're friends.

Narong: Yes. We always help each other.

Charoen: Thank you all. I'll try to settle my debt as soon as possible.

Wichian: That's true — I just remembered I have something to take care of too. Sorry.

Sombun: No problem at all. See you next time.

Thawi: Yes, see you again.

(Prani and Wichian leave the conversation)

Sombun: It's just the two of us now.

Thawi: Right. What should we do next?

Sombun: I think we should be considerate and look after our friends, like Prani who had to rush to submit documents.

Thawi: Exactly, sometimes we need to be understanding and help each other when necessary.

Sombun: It's normal for friends to have things to do; we should support one another.

Thawi: Right, as friends we should always be there for each other.

Sombun: Then let's keep looking around; maybe we'll find something Prani would like.

Thawi: Sounds good — let's go!

Wichian: Hey, I'm back!

Sombun: Oh, Wichian — you're back?

Thawi: Glad you're back! We were just about to keep looking around.

Wichian: Great, I'd like to look around too.

Sombun: By the way, have you ever bargained here?

Wichian: Sure. Sometimes they'll give a big discount.

Thawi: Really? I'm not very good at bargaining.

Wichian: Give it a try. Sometimes they'll lower the price because they want to sell.

Sombun: But sometimes you have to be careful. Some shops say it's discounted but they raised the price beforehand.

Thawi: Oh, true. I've experienced that too.

Wichian: Yes, we have to check carefully whether the discount is real.

Sombun: So we need to be cautious.

Wichian: Exactly, but I'm going to buy a coffee now.

Thawi: Okay, see you later.

Sombun: See you, Wichian.

Wichian: See you!

Prani: Hello everyone! I'm back.

Sombun: Oh, Prani! Welcome back.

Thawi: Glad you're back! We're looking at things.

Prani: Great. I saw an item in Sombun's shop that I'm really interested in.

Sombun: Really? Which one?

Prani: The amulet — I remember when you opened the shop I helped arrange for monks to come and bless the place.

Sombun: Yes, I remember. Thank you so much.

Prani: So, Sombun, can you give me a discount?

Sombun: Haha, sure, but you'll have to buy additional items to meet the promotion.

Thawi: Yeah, that way we can keep a good relationship.

Prani: Okay, okay, I understand. I'll look at more items too.

Sombun: Thank you so much for supporting my shop, Prani.

Prani: It's nothing. Friends should help each other.

Thawi: Exactly — as friends we should always support one another.

Prani: Then let's keep looking around.

Sombun: Let's go!

topic.scenario: At Bang Phut Community Health Center, Pak Kret, Nonthaburi
topic.situation_topic: Talking about physical therapy
topic.situation: Udom is weak and cannot move normally after being hospitalized for over three months, so he needs to receive physical therapy at the health center. But Udom strongly believes he doesn't need physical therapy and can recover without it.
topic.lie_objective: Concerned and doesn't want any problems
topic.leave_reason_B: Need to grab a snack or drink
topic.leave_reason_D_1: Need to charge the laptop
topic.leave_reason_D_2: Need to quickly set up the room before the next meeting

relationship: Udom, Thawi, and Somphon are Narong's family.
character_roles: Udom Thawi Somphon เป็นครอบครัวของ Narong

lie.real_reason_c: Udom will be uncooperative and will complain
lie.lie_c: At least you should go in and listen to the staff's advice
lie.truth_c: If you don't do physical therapy, recovery will be slow or may not happen at all

part_1:
Narong: Hello everyone. Have you all arrived?

Udom: Hello, Narong. Yes, we've arrived. How are you?

Thawi: Yes, Narong. You look tired. Is there anything I can help with?

Narong: Thank you, Thawi. I'm fine—just a bit busy here at the health center.

Somphon: Is it busy today, Narong?

Narong: Quite a bit, Somphon. A lot of people are coming for vaccinations lately.

Udom: That's good. We need to be careful these days.

Thawi: Yes. Health is the most important thing.

Somphon: So what do we need to do here, Narong?

Narong: I'll show you around first. There might also be some volunteer work organizing supplies.

Udom: Sounds good, Narong. We're happy to help.

Thawi: Yes, we're here to help make the community better.

Narong: Thank you all. Let's get started.

Somphon: Let's go!
part_2:
Udom: Sorry everyone, I need to grab a snack or a drink. I'll be right back.

Somphon: I need to charge my laptop. I'll be right back as well.

Narong: Okay, Udom, Somphon. See you later.

Thawi: All right. Now it's just the two of us, Narong.

Narong: That's right, Thawi. By the way, what do you think about Udom?

Thawi: Hmm... sometimes he seems not very interested in what we're doing.

Narong: I feel the same. Maybe he has other things to deal with.

Thawi: Yes. We might need to talk to him to help him understand more.

Narong: I agree. I think we should have an open conversation so we can understand each other better.

Thawi: I agree, Narong. Communication is the most important thing.

Narong: Thanks, Thawi, for understanding. Let's continue with the tasks.

Thawi: Okay, Narong. Let's go.
part_3:
Somphon: I'm back. Sorry I was gone so long.

Narong: Welcome back, Somphon. We're reviewing the tasks.

Thawi: Yes, we were just talking about physical therapy.

Somphon: Oh, that's great. I'm interested in that too.

Narong: Have you ever had physical therapy, Somphon?

Somphon: Yes. When I injured my leg last year, it helped a lot.

Thawi: That's right. Without physical therapy, recovery will be slow or may not happen at all.

Somphon: I agree. Physical therapy is very important.

Narong: How is your leg now?

Somphon: Much better, thank you for asking.

Thawi: That's good to hear.

Somphon: Thanks, but I need to quickly set up the room for the next meeting. Sorry.

Narong: No problem, Somphon. See you later.

Thawi: Good luck, Somphon.

Somphon: Thank you. See you.
part_4:
Udom: I'm back, everyone. Sorry I was gone so long.

Narong: Welcome back, Udom.

Thawi: Yes, Udom. You look tired.

Udom: Yeah, I've been feeling a bit exhausted lately.

Narong: Are you okay? Is there anything we can help with?

Udom: Thanks, Narong. I think I'm okay — I just need to rest a lot.

Thawi: Have you tried physical therapy?

Udom: Not yet. I think I can recover on my own.

Narong: But I think you should at least go in and listen to the staff's advice.

Thawi: Yes, Udom. We're worried about you and don't want problems in the future.

Udom: Thanks for your concern. I'll consider it.

Narong: Good. If you need anything, just let us know.

Udom: Thank you very much, everyone.

Amphon: The weather's nice today. Is everyone ready for the ancestral spirit-worship ceremony?

Somchai: Yes, I'm ready, Brother Amphon. I've prepared the offerings.

Prani: I'm ready too, but I'm not sure what to do. Nittaya, could you tell me?

Nittaya: Sure, Prani. We'll start by arranging the offerings, then light incense and candles to notify our ancestors.

Amphon: Yes, and don't forget to say the prayer. It's a way to show respect and thanks.

Somchai: I like this ceremony. I feel like it connects us with our ancestors.

Prani: Yes, it makes us feel warm and that it has a lot of meaning.

Nittaya: After that we'll eat together—sharing happiness as a family.

Amphon: Exactly. That's what makes us feel like one family.

Somchai: Then let's get started before we're late.

Prani: Let's go. I'm very excited.

Nittaya: Okay, let's arrange the offerings.
part_2:
Somchai: Sorry everyone, I'll step out to buy drinks. I'll be back soon.

Nittaya: I need to step away to make a phone call—there's an urgent matter I have to handle.

Amphon: All right, Somchai, Nittaya—see you later.

Prani: Okay, we'll wait here.

Amphon: Prani, do you think Somchai will be okay if we make any mistakes during the ceremony?

Prani: I don't think he'll mind, but I want everything to go as well as possible.

Amphon: Yes, I feel the same. We must try our best so everyone feels good.

Prani: I hope we can make everyone happy.

Amphon: Of course. We'll do our best to make the atmosphere warm and joyful.

Prani: Yes, I believe we can.

Amphon: Let's continue preparing, then.

Prani: Okay, let's go.

Prani: Yes, we're trying to decide what to make.

Prani: Yes, it should be fine.

Nittaya: I have to go drop off some documents—I just remembered there's urgent work.

Amphon: Okay, Nittaya. See you.

Prani: Yes, see you.

Nittaya: See you, everyone.

Sawat: That's right. Having everyone gather like this feels warm.

Samran: What can we do to help? I see there are many things that need to be arranged.

topic.scenario: On the back of an elephant in the ordination procession passing through Pring Village, Ba subdistrict, Tha Tum district, Surin province.
topic.situation_topic: Wearing dark sunglasses while the nak rides an elephant in very hot weather.
topic.situation: Udom, who was being ordained that year, was riding an elephant in the procession wearing dark sunglasses. By tradition, the nak must keep them on until reaching the ordination hall and only then remove them to symbolize seeing the light of the Dhamma. But because of the extreme heat, Udom felt very uncomfortable and overheated, especially from the sunglasses. Although Somphon had already taken off his glasses and told Udom to remove his as well, Udom hesitated because he was afraid his father would see and be disappointed, forbidding him to take them off and embarrassing him in front of the villagers. Somphon insisted nonetheless, not wanting his friend to faint during the ceremony.

Udom: Wow! This is my first time riding on an elephant in an ordination procession. I'm so excited!

Somphon: Definitely, Udom! I never thought I'd get to sit on an elephant like this. It's so high.

Nittaya: It's actually fun, but at first I was a bit scared I might fall off.

Amphon: Don't worry, Nittaya. The elephants here are well trained, and the mahouts are very skilled.

Udom: Yeah, I saw them controlling the elephants really well, and the atmosphere in the village is great.

Somphon: Everyone looks so happy; it makes me feel glad too.

Nittaya: Yes, everyone is smiling brightly, and there is also local music playing.

Amphon: I love the sound of the drums and the khaen; it really livens up the atmosphere.

Udom: Being at an event like this really makes you feel like part of the community.

Somphon: Exactly, Udom. Coming to events like this lets us learn more about the local culture.

Nittaya: And we've made new friends too. See how everyone smiles and greets each other?

Amphon: Yes. I think we should come to events like this more often. They're fun and we gain lots of new experiences.

Udom: I agree! Next time there's an event, we must come together again!

Udom: Okay, see you.

Nittaya: Safe travels to both of you.

Nittaya: Yes, and if something did happen, we would have to take responsibility together.

Udom: Exactly. We're friends, so we have to look out for each other.

Nittaya: Yes, Udom. I'm glad to have friends like this.

Udom: Welcome back, Amphon! We were just talking about wearing dark sunglasses while the nak rides an elephant in very hot weather.

Udom: Thank you so much, Somphon. I'm lucky to have friends like you.

Nittaya: Exactly. We all have to take care of one another.

Somphon: Of course. We're friends, so we should always help each other.

topic.scenario: On the back of an elephant in the ordination procession passing through Pring Village, Ba Subdistrict, Tha Tum District, Surin Province.
topic.situation_topic: Wearing sunglasses while the novice rides an elephant in very hot weather.
topic.situation: That year Sombat, who was being ordained, was riding an elephant in the procession while wearing dark sunglasses. By tradition, symbolizing ignorance, the novice must keep them on until they reach the ordination hall and only then remove them to show the light of the Dhamma. But because of the extreme heat, Sombat felt very uncomfortable and overheated, especially from the sunglasses. Although Charoen had already taken his off and told Sombat to remove his as well, Sombat hesitated because he was afraid his father would see, be disappointed, and strictly forbid him from taking them off, embarrassing him in front of the villagers. Charoen insisted, however, that he didn't want his friend to faint during the ceremony.
topic.lie_objective: To avoid conflict.
topic.leave_reason_B: Take a coffee break.
topic.leave_reason_D_1: Want to go buy a drink.
topic.leave_reason_D_2: Need to handle an urgent email.

part_1:
Sombat: Wow! The atmosphere is really nice. The ordination procession here is beautiful.

Charoen: That's right, Sombat! This is the first time I've come to see the procession in Surin. I'm really excited.

Udom: Me too. I like the live traditional music — it's so pleasant to listen to.

Prasoet: Do you guys know the name of the elephant we're sitting on?

Sombat: I don't know. Prasoet, do you?

Prasoet: I do. This elephant is called Phlai Thong. It's well-known in this village.

Charoen: Wow! That's a nice name. Have any of you ridden an elephant before?

Udom: I rode once when I was a child, but I don't remember much.

Sombat: I've never ridden one. This is my first time — I'm very excited.

Prasoet: Don't be afraid, Sombat. The elephants here are very tame and well cared for.

Charoen: Yeah. So where do you think we should go after this?

Udom: I think we should eat at the village market. I've heard there's lots of delicious food.

Sombat: I agree. I'm hungry too.

Prasoet: Then it's settled. After the procession we'll go.

Charoen: Okay! Let's enjoy the procession!
part_2:
Charoen: Excuse me everyone, I'm going to take a quick coffee break. I'll be back.

Prasoet: I'll go buy some drinks too. I'll be back as well.

Sombat: Okay, see you.

Udom: Sombat, what do you think Charoen will feel if his friends don't follow his advice?

Sombat: Hmm... I think Charoen might feel bad because he usually has good ideas.

Sombat: That's true. It's something to think about carefully. But I think Charoen won't be angry — he's a kind person.

Udom: Let's hope so. Still, we should listen to our friends' advice sometimes.

Sombat: That's right. We should value everyone's opinions.

Udom: Yeah, let's wait for Charoen and Prasoet to come back, then we'll continue.

Sombat: Sure. Then we'll go eat at the village market as planned.

Sombat: But I'm still wearing mine. I'm afraid my father will see and be displeased.

Sombat: Thanks, Charoen. If there's a problem, I'll tell you.

Udom: That's right. We're together — we can help each other.

Charoen: Good. Let's enjoy the ceremony.

Sombat: Sounds good!

According to the traditional custom of avijja (symbolizing ignorance), the candidate must keep the glasses on until reaching the ordination hall, then remove them to show that he has seen the light of Dhamma. But because it was extremely hot, Chan felt very uncomfortable and overheated, especially because of the dark glasses. Although Sombun had already taken off his own sunglasses and told Chan to take his off too, Chan hesitated—afraid his father would see, be disappointed, and forbid him from removing them, shaming him before the villagers. Sombun insisted, however, that his friend should not faint during the ceremony.
topic.lie_objective: To avoid conflict.

part_1:
Chan: Wow! This is the first time I've ever sat on an elephant's back in an ordination procession like this.

Sombun: That's right! The atmosphere is great—there's music and lots of villagers taking part.

Prasoet: I love how beautifully everyone is dressed. Look, everyone's traditional Thai outfits are really lovely.

Prasit: Yes, and the elephant walks so gracefully, like it knows it's part of an important ceremony.

Chan: I'm so excited to be part of this ordination procession. It's a truly unique experience.

Sombun: Exactly, and coming to an event like this with friends makes it even better.

Prasoet: Actually, I think we should take part in events like this more often. It helps us learn about our culture and traditions.

Prasit: I agree. It also gives us time together as friends and brings us closer.

Chan: So let's promise to join this every year, okay?

Sombun: Sounds great! I totally agree.

Prasoet: Me too! Let's meet here again next year.

Prasit: Of course! See you again next year, and we'll make it an even better experience.

Sombun: Sorry everyone, I need to check an email quickly. I'll be right back.

Prasit: I have to use the restroom too. I'll be right back.

Chan: Okay, see you soon.

Prasoet: By the way, Chan, how do you think Sombun will feel if his friends don't follow his advice?

Prasoet: Exactly, I think so too. If anything happened, no one would want to take responsibility.

Chan: Actually, it's important to listen to friends' advice sometimes, especially if it's about safety.

Chan: Oh, Prasit, you're back? Sombun still hasn't come back.

Chan: But why don't you take them off sometimes?

part_4:
Sombun: I'm back, everyone! Sorry I was gone so long.

Chan: Welcome back, Sombun! Did you take off your sunglasses?

Sombun: Yes, I took them off. It's so hot. Chan, why don't you try taking yours off?

Chan: I want to, but my father said not to take them off until we reach the ordination hall.

Prasoet: But if you're really uncomfortable, you could rest your eyes for a bit.

Sombun: Right, Chan. If you're feeling unwell, you should rest your eyes. I don't want you fainting during the ceremony.

Chan: Thanks, Sombun. I'll think about it again.

Prasoet: Exactly, Chan. Safety is the most important thing.

Chan: I understand. Thanks for worrying about me, everyone.

Sombun: It's nothing. We're friends, so we should help each other.

Prasoet: That's right. We'll get through today together.

Chan: Thank you all so much. I feel much better.

topic.scenario: In front of the shop in an Akha village, Chiang Rai province, at noon on the third day of the swing ceremony
topic.situation_topic: Spending money to buy items is prohibited during the two days after the swing festival, but receiving money is not prohibited
topic.situation: During the festival period when spending money is forbidden, Sawat decided to break custom by secretly buying a silver necklace to replace an heirloom that had gone missing. He hoped to use it as an amulet for good luck during the swing ceremony before traveling for work elsewhere. But his action was not a secret when Sombat happened to see it and confronted him out of concern about the curse from offending spirits and the disgrace that would follow if the villagers found out.

Sawat: (smiles) Hello everyone. The weather is nice today.

Sombat: Yes, Sawat. The weather is pleasantly cool — perfect for a walk around the village.

Wichai: Hello Sawat, Sombat. There's the swing ceremony today — are you coming to watch?

Somchai: Yes. Today is the third day. This ceremony is a lot of fun.

Sawat: Of course. We came specifically to watch. What does this ceremony mean?

Wichai: The swing ceremony is a celebration of the Akha people. It's a way to thank the spirits for a good harvest this year.

Sombat: That sounds very interesting. Are you both taking part in the ceremony?

Somchai: Yes. We'll be helping prepare food and drinks for the attendees.

Sawat: That's great. Can we help with anything?

Wichai: Thank you. If you'd like to help, you can come and set the food tables.

Sombat: Sure. We'll do our best to help.

Somchai: Thank you. You are very kind.

Sawat: Glad to. We came here to learn and to take part in the local culture.

Wichai: Welcome. I hope you enjoy the swing ceremony.

Sombat: Thank you, Wichai and Somchai. We're looking forward to seeing the ceremony.

Somchai: I have to go feed the animals. See you later.

Sawat: Okay, Sombat and Somchai — see you later.

Wichai: Now it's just the two of us, Sawat.

Sawat: Yes, Wichai. I heard Sombat has something to tell everyone in the village, and it turned into a big issue.

Wichai: Oh, that? I heard about it too. It seems to be something people in the village are talking about a lot.

Sawat: Right. I'm curious what the truth actually is.

Wichai: I think Sombat must have his reasons, but sometimes speaking plainly can lead others to misunderstand.

Sawat: True. Some topics need caution when discussed, or they can blow up into something bigger.

Wichai: Yes, but I believe Sombat didn't mean for it to become like that.

Sawat: I think so too. I hope it resolves well.

Wichai: Same here. We'll probably find out the truth soon.

Sawat: Yes. Thanks for talking with me, Wichai.

Wichai: You're welcome, Sawat. Let's go help set the food tables.

Sawat: Sounds good. Let's go.

Sawat: Welcome back, Somchai.

Wichai: You're back quickly, Somchai.

Somchai: Thanks. I finished feeding the animals sooner than expected.

Sawat: Great. We're about to go help set the food tables.

Sawat: Was the necklace pretty?

topic.scenario: On the sandy courtyard under the Sri (Bodhi) tree in front of the Hoeng Luang viharn
topic.situation_topic: The custom that the number of raffle strips must equal the number of raffle bundles
topic.situation: Somsak was assigned to write and count his family's raffle strips to be piled together in front of the viharn. But through carelessness Somsak dropped 2–3 strips or miscounted, causing the total not to match the number of raffle bundles arranged — which violates the strict rule forbidding any shortage or excess, because if a monk finds an empty slip it would cause problems. Thawi walked over to inspect and asked again whether the count of strips matched the bundles.

part_1:
Prasit: What dishes do we have today?

Wichian: Today we have green curry chicken and mixed stir-fried vegetables, Prasit.

Somphon: And for dessert there's bua loi in ginger syrup.

Sombun: Oh right, I forgot. I need to prepare the bua loi dough.

Prasit: Good. I'll check the green curry first. Wichian, please watch the stir-fry.

Wichian: Sure, Prasit. I'll take care of it.

Somphon: Sombun, let's go shape the bua loi together.

Sombun: Okay, Somphon. We need to hurry; people are starting to come.

Prasit: Don't forget to taste the flavors, everyone. Make sure it's delicious.

Wichian: Yes, Prasit. I'll taste it to make sure it's really good.

Somphon: I'll taste the bua loi.

Sombun: I'll get the ginger syrup ready.

Prasit: Thanks, everyone. If you need anything, tell me.

Wichian: Yes, Prasit. We'll do our best.

Somphon: Yes, we'll make everyone who comes to eat happy.

Sombun: Exactly. We must do our best for the Pak Heuang shrine.

Prasit: Very good, everyone. Let's get to it!
part_2:
Prasit: Sorry everyone, I need to step out for a moment. There's an urgent matter.

Sombun: I have to excuse myself too. I'm not feeling well—probably a mild allergic reaction.

Wichian: It's okay, Prasit and Sombun. Please rest and get better.

Somphon: Yes, take care of yourself, Sombun.

Prasit: Thanks, everyone. I'll be back.

Sombun: Thank you. I'll come back quickly to help.

(Prasit and Sombun leave the conversation)

Wichian: Somphon, we need to be careful about that pot. If it's really ruined we'll have to make it again.

Somphon: Yes. If the flavor is truly off, we'll have to pour it out and start over.

Wichian: Prasit probably won't be angry if we did our best.

Somphon: Right. We must ensure the food we serve is tasty and safe.

Wichian: Let's taste it again. If it's not okay, we can fix it quickly.

Somphon: Agreed. I'll prepare backup ingredients in case we need them.

Wichian: Good idea. We need to be ready for any situation.

Somphon: Yes, we'll do our best for everyone who comes to eat.

Wichian: Alright, let's keep going!
part_3:
Sombun: I'm back, everyone.

Wichian: Welcome back, Sombun. Are you feeling better?

Sombun: I'm better now, thank you.

Somphon: Glad you're back. We were just about to taste the food.

Sombun: Oh, that's good, but I just remembered we have a rule forbidding tasting food prepared as offerings to the Pak Heuang spirit.

Wichian: That's true—I forgot.

Somphon: Then we need to be extra careful.

Sombun: Yes, we must strictly follow the rule.

Wichian: Thanks for the reminder, Sombun.

Somphon: Yes, thank you.

Sombun: You're welcome. I need to step out and water the plants now.

Wichian: Okay, Sombun.

Somphon: Take good care of the plants, please.

Sombun: Thanks. I'll be off then.

(Sombun leaves the conversation)

topic.scenario: At the free food kitchen beside the Chao Pho Pak Hueang shrine
topic.situation_topic: Rule forbidding tasting food prepared as an offering to Chao Pho Pak Hueung
topic.situation: While preparing a large pot of water-buffalo larb to offer to Chao Pho Pak Hueung and to serve guests, Thawi absentmindedly scooped some larb liquid and touched his tongue to taste it. This was a serious breach of the strict rule that forbids tasting before offering. Somsak happened to see the moment Thawi brought the spoon to his mouth and asked whether he had tasted it.
topic.lie_objective: To protect the ritual from being tainted and to avoid having the entire pot ordered to be thrown away
topic.leave_reason_B: Needed to deal with family matters
topic.leave_reason_D_1: Remembered there was something that needed taking care of
topic.leave_reason_D_2: Forgot to print a document

part_1:
Thawi: There are so many people today, Sis Somsak.

Somsak: Yes, Thawi. Today is an important day, so many people came to make merit.

Somphon: Sis Somsak, which dish should we start with?

Somsak: Start with the green curry first, Somphon. I'll take care of the curry paste.

Narong: Sis Somsak, what can I help with?

Somsak: Narong, help Thawi cut the vegetables. I'll check on the curry pot.

Thawi: Sure, Narong. Let's get started.

Somphon: Sis Somsak, do we have enough curry paste, or should I go buy more?

Somsak: It's enough, Somphon. If there are leftovers, we can save them for next time.

Narong: Thawi, is the chopped vegetable amount enough?

Thawi: It's enough, Narong. Thanks a lot.

Somsak: Everyone is doing great. We must finish on time today.

Somphon: Don't worry, Sis Somsak. We'll all help as much as we can.

Narong: Yes, we'll make the food as delicious as possible.

Somsak: Thank you all. I'm glad to have your help.
part_2:
Somsak: Sorry everyone, I have to go deal with a family matter. Please take care of things while I'm gone.

Narong: I have to go too. I just remembered there's something I need to handle. Sorry about that.

Thawi: That's okay, Sis Somsak. Narong, Somphon and I will take over.

Somphon: Yes, don't worry. We'll handle everything properly.

Somsak: Thank you so much. See you later.

Narong: Thanks. See you.

(After Somsak and Narong leave the conversation)

Thawi: Somphon, do you think Sis Somsak will be angry if that pot has to be thrown away?

Somphon: I'm thinking the same, but we'll just have to make it again and make it better.

Thawi: Right. We have to be more careful this time and not make the same mistake.

Somphon: Let's start again then. I'll help with the curry paste.

Thawi: Thanks a lot, Somphon. We'll do our best.

Somphon: Of course, Thawi. We won't let Sis Somsak down.

Thawi: That's right. Let's make this a success!
part_3:
Narong: I'm back, everyone. Sorry I was gone so long.

Thawi: Welcome back, Narong. We were just starting to remake the food.

Somphon: Yes, Narong. We need to make it better than before.

Narong: Great. Is there anything you need me to do?

Thawi: Actually, we were talking about the rule that forbids tasting food prepared as an offering to Chao Pho Pak Hueung.

Narong: Oh, yes. I heard that tasting is strictly forbidden.

Somphon: But... I have something to tell you. I accidentally tasted it already.

Thawi: Really, Somphon? What are we going to do?

Narong: Oh wow, that's a big problem.

Somphon: I feel really bad, but we'll just have to make it again and do it better.

part_1:
Udom: What are we making today?

Narong: Today we'll make chicken green curry and stir-fried mixed vegetables, Udom.

Thawi: And dessert, Udom?

Udom: Dessert today is bua loy in ginger syrup.

Somphon: Wow, bua loy in ginger syrup is my favorite!

Narong: Shall we start prepping?

Udom: Okay. Narong, help chop the vegetables; Thawi, prepare the chicken.

Thawi: Got it, Udom. I'll finish quickly.

Somphon: What should I do, Udom?

Udom: Somphon, watch the green curry pot—don't let it boil over.

Somphon: Understood, Udom.

Narong: Udom, where should I put the chopped vegetables?

Udom: Put them in that large tray. We'll use them for stir-frying.

Thawi: The chicken's ready, Udom.

Udom: Great, Thawi. Let's start stir-frying.

Somphon: The green curry pot is smelling good.

Udom: Good job, Somphon. We'll be able to serve the guests soon.

Narong: There are a lot of people today.

Thawi: Yes, I see a long line waiting for food.

Udom: Then we all have to hurry. Let's go!
part_2:
Udom: Sorry everyone, I have to go get snacks and drinks. I'll be back.

Somphon: I need to charge my laptop first. I'll be back.

Narong: Okay, Udom and Somphon.

Thawi: Let's continue talking then. Narong, do you think the green curry we're making will be okay?

Narong: I hope so, but if it's really bad, Udom might not be pleased.

Thawi: Right. If we have to dump it and redo it, that would waste a lot of time.

Narong: We have to be more careful, Thawi. Don't let that happen.

Thawi: Yes, we'll take good care.

Narong: I'll go check the green curry pot again.

Thawi: Great, I'll keep an eye on the stir-fry.

Narong: Thanks so much, Thawi. We have to do our best for Udom.

Thawi: Yes, we'll make sure everyone is impressed.
part_3:
Somphon: I'm back, everyone.

Narong: Welcome back, Somphon.

Thawi: Somphon, we were just talking about the rule forbidding tasting food offered to Chao Pho Pak Heuang.

Somphon: Oh yes. That rule is very strict.

Narong: Yes, but sometimes I wonder what would happen if we did taste it.

Thawi: Actually, I once tasted it, but I didn't tell anyone.

Somphon: Whoa, Thawi! Be careful. If Udom finds out, it won't go over well.

Narong: Right. We need to be more careful.

Thawi: I know, but it smelled so good at the time.

Somphon: I understand, but be careful next time.

Narong: Somphon, do you need to go anywhere else?

Somphon: Yes, I need to quickly set up the room before the next meeting. Excuse me.

Thawi: Okay, Somphon. See you later.

topic.situation_topic: The five pungent vegetables forbidden during the Vegetarian Festival
topic.situation: While Amphon was stirring a large pot of mixed boiled vegetables (a big pot meant for distributing to thousands), he accidentally dropped fried garlic into the pot. This violates the Vegetarian Festival rule forbidding the five pungent vegetables, which are said to destroy the fire element, and it immediately contaminates that vegetarian dish. Udom came to check, smelled something odd, and asked if anything had fallen into the pot.

Prasoet: Right, I want to help as much as I can.

Udom: Thank you all. Having you help makes our work go much faster.

Prasoet: Yes, we'll all do our best to help.

Nittaya: That's right. Udom would feel bad if there's a lot of leftover food.

Amphon: I agree. We should manage it well so nothing gets wasted.

Nittaya: Yes. We need to calculate portions accurately so nothing goes to waste.

Nittaya: Yes, Udom won't have to worry about this as much.

topic.scenario: At the courtyard in front of Kiriwong Temple (Ban Hua Khao Chin), Pak Tho District, Ratchaburi Province
topic.situation_topic: Rules for reserving a partner using the luk chuang
topic.situation: Narong secretly likes a girl named Nang Taeng, but Narong's friend threw a luk chuang to her and caught it from her first, which by the rules counts as having reserved her. Annoyed, Narong purposely threw his own luk chuang to hit his friend's luk chuang in her hand so it fell, disrupting the moment. Chan saw the commotion and came to question Narong whether he intentionally threw the top to steal the partner.

topic.leave_reason_B: Need to attend to a person who just arrived.
topic.leave_reason_D_1: Need to check on an urgent important matter.
topic.leave_reason_D_2: Suddenly remembered I have to deal with paperwork.

Narong: Hello everyone. My name is Narong. I'm from out of town. I'm here to perform in a concert today.

Chan: Welcome, Narong. I'm Chan, the head of the ring here. If you need anything, just let me know.

Nittaya: Hello, Narong. I'm Nittaya, Narong's friend.

Somchit: Yes. I'm Somchit, another friend. Nice to meet you.

Narong: Thank you all. The atmosphere here is really nice.

Chan: That's right. The courtyard in front of Kiriwong Temple is a place people like to come relax.

Nittaya: What songs will you perform today, Narong?

Narong: I have some new songs I wrote myself, and also some well-known songs.

Somchit: Sounds interesting. I can't wait to hear them.

Chan: If you need anything else, just say. We have the equipment ready.

Narong: Thank you, Chan. I feel very welcomed to meet everyone here.

Nittaya: Glad you feel that way, Narong. Hope the concert will be fun.

Somchit: Yes. We'll be cheering in the front.

Narong: Thank you all. I'll do my best!
part_2:
Chan: Sorry everyone, I have to attend to someone who just arrived. Enjoy the concert.

Somchit: I also have to check on an urgent important matter. Sorry everyone.

Narong: It's okay. Thanks for stopping by to say hello.

Nittaya: Yes, thank you very much. See you again.

(Chan and Somchit leave the conversation)

Narong: Nittaya, let's continue talking.

Nittaya: Sure, Narong. By the way, Chan seemed busy.

Narong: Yes, he's taking care of a lot, but he's doing it well.

Nittaya: That's true. But I heard that if anyone breaks the rules here, they might not be allowed to come back.

Narong: Hmm, yes. This place is quite strict about rules.

Nittaya: That's understandable, they need to maintain order.

Narong: Right, I hope everyone understands and follows the rules.

Nittaya: I believe if everyone cooperates, the event will go well.

Narong: Exactly. Let's make today a great day together.

Nittaya: Of course, Narong. I'll be cheering up front!
part_3:
Narong: Oh, Somchit, you're back?

Somchit: Yes, I'm back, but I have to go again soon.

Nittaya: Nice to see you again, Somchit.

Somchit: Thank you, Nittaya. By the way, what were you talking about?

Narong: We were talking about the rules for reserving a partner with the luk chuang.

Somchit: Ah, that's important. If you don't follow the rules, problems can arise.

Nittaya: Yes. I've heard that someone intentionally threw their luk chuang to interfere with a friend out of jealousy.

Somchit: Really? That's not good.

Narong: Yes, doing that is unacceptable.

Somchit: I agree. Everyone should play fair.

Nittaya: Right. We should have fun together.

Somchit: Sorry, I just remembered I have to handle some paperwork. Excuse me.

Narong: It's okay, Somchit. Thanks for talking with us.

Nittaya: Yes, thank you very much. See you again.

Somchit: Okay, see you everyone!
part_4:
Chan: Hello everyone, I'm back. Is there anything I can help with?

Narong: Oh, hello Chan. Nothing much, just chatting.

Nittaya: Yes, just talking about general things.

Chan: Hmm, but I noticed something happened over there earlier.

Narong: Oh, that. It was just an accident.

Nittaya: That's right, Chan. It was nothing—just the luk chuang slipped out of someone's hand.

Chan: Are you sure? Because I saw what looked like someone throwing a luk chuang to hit another.

Narong: Uh... it might have looked intentional, but it really wasn't.

Nittaya: Yes, it happened so quickly—no one meant for that to happen.

Chan: If that's the case, okay. But please be careful—don't let this happen again.

Narong: Yes. I'm sorry. I'll be more careful.

Nittaya: Thank you, Chan, for understanding.

Chan: It's all right. Just be cautious.

Narong: Yes, thank you very much for understanding.

Nittaya: Yes, thank you so much, Chan.

topic.scenario: At the courtyard in front of Kiriwong Temple (Ban Hua Khao Jeen), Pak Tho District, Ratchaburi Province
topic.situation_topic: Rules for reserving a partner using the 'luk-chuang' (tossed ring)
topic.situation: Wichian secretly has a crush on a woman named Nang Taeng. But Wichian's friend tossed a luk-chuang to Nang Taeng and received the luk-chuang from her first — under the rule that counts as having claimed her. Out of jealousy, Wichian threw his own luk-chuang to strike his friend's luk-chuang in Nang Taeng's hand so it flew out of her hand, disrupting the moment. Udom saw the commotion and came over to question Wichian whether he intentionally threw his luk-chuang to hit his friend in order to steal the partner.

topic.leave_reason_D_1: There is an urgent matter to deal with
topic.leave_reason_D_2: Need to go meet someone for a moment
